description: A structured-finance director must approve and finalize a proposed receivables securitization, including its legal isolation, credit enhancement, investor-facing note structure, and servicing controls, with input from legal, risk, investor coverage, and loan operations.

shared_context.S1: The bank is considering a securitization of $60,000,000 of consumer receivables.
shared_context.S2: The preliminary term sheet proposes a four-year transaction with a 2% reserve, a 5% delinquency trigger, monthly servicer remittances, and no special note-rating condition.
shared_context.S3: Maya has authority to approve the transaction and issue the final term sheet.
shared_context.S4: At the scheduled term-sheet review, Maya follows the bank's routine sign-off process by asking legal, credit risk, investor coverage, and loan operations to state any condition that must be reflected before approval.

PF1.text: Elias received a legal memorandum this morning stating that counsel can deliver a true-sale opinion only if the receivables are transferred to a bankruptcy-remote special-purpose vehicle and the seller has no recourse for ordinary pool losses; the memorandum has not yet been attached to the term-sheet file.

PF2.text: Nora completed the portfolio stress review this week and confirmed that approval requires an initial cash reserve of exactly $3,500,000 and an early-amortization trigger at exactly 4% delinquency; her risk worksheet is still in draft circulation.

PF3.text: Victor confirmed in the anchor investor's mandate received yesterday that the investor may buy only rated notes with a weighted-average life of no more than exactly 18 months; he has not yet uploaded the mandate extract to the transaction room.

PF4.text: Grace confirmed with the servicer this morning that weekly remittances are operationally supported only with a 30-day cutover notice and a named backup servicer designated before closing; the operations checklist has not yet been updated.

acceptance_conditions: The receivables must be transferred through a bankruptcy-remote special-purpose vehicle.
The seller must have no recourse for ordinary pool losses.
The initial cash reserve must be exactly $3,500,000.
The early-amortization delinquency trigger must be exactly 4%.
Only rated notes may be offered and their weighted-average life must not exceed 18 months.
The servicer must receive exactly 30 days' cutover notice.
A backup servicer must be designated before closing.

decisive_facts.why: The preliminary term sheet does not require a special-purpose vehicle or eliminate seller recourse; PF1 changes both legal structure decisions and creates the true-sale-legal-opinion commitment.
The draft uses a 2% reserve and 5% delinquency trigger; PF2 changes the exact reserve to $3,500,000 and the exact trigger to 4%.
The draft has no rating requirement and offers a four-year structure; PF3 changes the note package to rated notes with a maximum weighted-average life of exactly 18 months.

The draft specifies monthly remittances with no transition controls; PF4 changes operations to weekly remittances, exactly 30 days of cutover notice, and designation of a backup servicer before closing.
